result.title: Graph-to-Table Interfaces Control Relational Generalisation
result.summary: Graph-to-table systems combine three design choices: an encoder that maps relational evidence to feature rows, a context constructor that selects labelled examples, and a tabular decoder. We investigate whether these components can be evaluated independently through matched comparisons that change one component while holding the rest of the pipeline and the evaluation constant. Across logistic regression, CATBOOST, and TABPFN-3 on CLUTRR, 57 GraphLog worlds, and 57 knowledge graphs, we show that conclusions about one component can change when the others change. On CLUTRR, absolute positional encodings maintain all distinctions among the evaluated queries and fit the short-path setting nearly perfectly; yet, they generalise worse than relation-count features because the supported prefix acts as a shortcut that breaks down on longer paths. On GraphLog, encoder preference depends on the decoder, while the relation-count representation degrades as CatBoost tree depth increases. Across different knowledge graphs, adding the frozen ULTRA score to local features is consistently useful, whereas adding local features to the score has a smaller and less stable effect. A pointwise TABPFN-3 readout using the full encoder underperforms native ULTRA on 48 of 57 datasets. These results show that encoder assessment depends jointly on context and decoder, while panel-level conclusions can also depend on evaluation and aggregation protocols.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 graph-to-table 系统（encoder、context constructor、tabular decoder）能否通过只改一个组件的匹配比较独立评估，并在 CLUTRR、GraphLog 及 57 个知识图谱上结合多种模型检验结论是否随其他组件和评估协议变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「组件优劣依赖 decoder、context 与聚合协议，无法独立归因」以及位置编码成为捷径、在长路径上失效的观察，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态与 readout 的贡献分配及长度泛化评价提供概念借鉴，具体对应关系仍需核查。
